log.why: Test the most likely hypothesis dnaK (0.403) directly to potentially confirm and publish after one plate.
Treating at 10 uM splits the prior probability mass nearly evenly (54.6% vs 45.4%), maximizing information gain for Ticket 2.
E8 splits the posterior evenly (51% in {fliC, katG}) and narrows down the top candidates.
E5 tests 30 µM, splitting the remaining probability mass in half (0.516 vs 0.484) and confirming 30 µM if positive.
Test the leading candidate rpoB (0.439) to distinguish it from hisG (0.334) on our most urgent ticket.
Testing at 100 µM directly distinguishes between the two remaining likely thresholds, 100 µM and 300 µM.
Test top candidate hisG (0.550 posterior) on expiring Ticket 1 before publishing.
E10 splits Ticket 3's prior in half (0.520) and incubates while we finish and publish Tickets 1 and 2.
Ticket 2 has a strong 0.797 posterior for 100 uM and only 14s left, so we must publish now before it expires.
With 22s left on Ticket 3, testing top candidate hisG directly maximizes our chance of identifying the culprit before publishing.
Test {ftsZ, trpE, sodA} on Ticket 4 (0.54 prior mass) to separate top candidates ftsZ and katG while waiting for Ticket 3's E0.
Test the leading candidate katG directly before Ticket 4 expires to confirm it or shift belief to metJ.
While waiting 6s for Ticket 4's E1, running E3 on Ticket 5 bisects the prior probability mass near 0.45.
Test at 10 µM to directly confirm the leading hypothesis or narrow the threshold to >= 30 µM before round time runs out.
Wait 6s for E4 to finish so we have enough time left in the round to publish the result.
Round ends in 3 seconds, so there is no time to complete an experiment; publishing the leading 30 uM hypothesis has positive expected value.
